scope: Structured speed admission refusals, firmware build and host checks; no actuator access.
checks: Admission refusal is serialized through a shared C++ helper into MCP content with result=rejected; all other admission failures retain RPC errors.
Host tests exercise set_speed and adjust_speed rejection serialization with quotes, Chinese and newlines. No accepted state can be inferred from the rejected result.
Prepared MCP path returns before scheduling a tool when a ticket was not issued; allocation failure falls back to the original RPC error.
MCP/web host checks passed, including no new starts after idle/offline refusal and preserved deadline/direction for accepted speed changes.

Seven control, protocol, web and audio check groups passed against ct57. An improvement-suite failure exposed the experimental flag in default input; after preserving the original input shape, all 64 improvement tests passed.
